subject: Unable to connect to local database after deploying the app on Shinyapps.io, HELP!

messages.author: 0c5b9950c4d8cfa4
messages.subject: Unable to connect to local database after deploying the app on Shinyapps.io, HELP!
parts:
Hi, 

 I was able to run my shiny app locally but I was unable to launch it in browser after successfully deploying the app. Thank you in advance! The Chrome browser says like this: 
RS-DBI driver: (could not connect shiny@localhost on dbname "dbname"

 




Local working app 



My server.R:
require('rCharts')
require('shiny')
library(lubridate)
library(RPostgreSQL)
library(quantmod)
require(zoo)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

      timeInterval<-c("Monthly","Weekly","Daily","Hourly")

getCon <- function(){

   drv <- dbDriver("PostgreSQL")
   con <- dbConnect(drv, dbname="dbname", host ="localhost", port=5432)

   ####Some function for accessing the databse#####
  return(order) #### return some dataset
}

sourceData <-reactive({

   order<-getCon()   

   #manipulate the order based on the selectInput
   
   return(order)
})

   #Drop down selection of time interval 
  output$choose_time_interval <- renderUI({
    selectInput("time_interval", "Choose a time interval", as.list(c(timeInterval,"15min")),selected="Daily")
  })

output$graph <- renderPlot({ 
  total_oder<-sourceData()

   #plot the order dataset

   })

My ui.R:
require('rCharts')
require('shiny')
library(lubridate)
library(RPostgreSQL)
library(quantmod)
require(zoo)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
 
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel('Dashboard'),
  
  sidebarPanel(
  uiOutput("choose_time_interval")
  ),
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput('graph')
  )
))

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Unable to connect to local database after deploying the app on Shinyapps.io, HELP!
parts:
Hi Jim,
The problem is that your application is looking to connect to a database on local host.  You probably have a database running on your own machine, but Shinyapps.io doesn't have your database.  You will need to either open a connection to your database from the outside world, bundle the data you are pulling out of the DB into CSV or RData files, or move your database to a service that can be reached remotely.  

Hope this helps.
